articles.title: Community Fun Day in Heywood Attracts Over 450 Residents
articles.excerpt: More than 450 local residents attended a community fun day in Heywood, organised by Rochdale Youth Service, featuring free food and various activities.
articles.content_html:
A community fun day in Heywood drew more than 450 local residents over the weekend. The event was organised by Rochdale Youth Service and offered a range of free food and activities.

Attendees enjoyed fun physical sessions, a bouncy castle, henna artistry, and various art activities. The event aimed to bring the community together and provide a day of entertainment for families.

Rochdale Youth Service facilitated the event to promote community engagement and provide a platform for local residents to connect with one another.

The success of the fun day highlights the interest in community events and the importance of such gatherings in fostering local relationships.

articles.title: Man jailed after arriving at Heywood school with weapons
articles.excerpt: A failed asylum seeker has been sentenced to two years in prison after taking a hammer, hatchet and kitchen knife to Edgar Wood Academy in Heywood, intending to create a scene for attention.
articles.content_html:
A failed asylum seeker has been jailed for two years after taking a hammer, a hatchet and a kitchen knife to a school in Heywood. Both Douk Deng, 21, from South Sudan, intended to 'create a scene for attention' to aid his immigration case, Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court heard.

Deng became increasingly frustrated with the lack of assistance from immigration authorities regarding his asylum applications, which had been refused three times. He was arrested on August 6 last year after workmen at Edgar Wood Academy confronted him on the premises.

A member of the public had alerted the authorities after seeing Deng behaving oddly while carrying a petrol can and a hammer tied to his belt. He was observed walking a full circuit around the school, which was closed to pupils for the summer, before builders called the police due to their concerns.

Deng was reported to be mumbling as he approached the school, prompting the workmen to take action. His actions were described as an attempt to draw attention to his situation.

articles.title: Two men injured in Heywood crash
articles.excerpt: Two men were taken to hospital with serious injuries following a crash involving two cars on Moss Hall Road in Heywood.
articles.content_html:
A crash involving two cars occurred on Moss Hall Road in Heywood at around 7.45am on Tuesday, July 28. Two men, aged 35 and 44, were taken to hospital with serious injuries, according to a spokesperson for Greater Manchester Police.

Emergency services, including police and paramedics, attended the scene. An air ambulance also landed nearby. Residents reported that a section of the road was closed for several hours following the incident.

Officers from Greater Manchester Police's Serious Collision Investigation Unit are investigating the crash. They have requested that anyone who witnessed the incident or has relevant footage, such as CCTV or dashcam recordings, come forward with information.

Anyone with information can contact police on 0161 856 4741 or via the Live Chat service, quoting log 616 of 28/07/26. Alternatively, information can be reported anonymously to Crimestoppers at 0800 555 111.

articles.title: Appeal for Information Following Serious Collision in Heywood
articles.excerpt: Officers from the Serious Collision Investigation Unit are seeking information after a collision between two vehicles on Moss Hall Road, Heywood, on Tuesday morning.
articles.content_html:
Officers from the Serious Collision Investigation Unit (SCIU) are appealing for information following a serious collision in Heywood.

The incident occurred on Moss Hall Road around 7:45am on Tuesday, 28 July, involving two vehicles. Emergency services responded to the scene shortly after the collision.

Authorities are urging anyone who witnessed the collision or has relevant information to come forward to assist with the investigation.

Anyone with information can find Greater Manchester Police and Crimestoppers contact details at the end of this article.

articles.title: Roadworks on Birtle Road in Heywood to Begin on 24 August 2026
articles.excerpt: Birtle Road in Heywood will undergo roadworks from 24 to 28 August 2026, resulting in a temporary closure affecting traffic flow.
articles.content_html:
Birtle Road in Heywood will be temporarily closed for roadworks from Monday, 24 August 2026, to Friday, 28 August 2026. The closure will take place daily from 10am to 4pm.

The affected section of Birtle Road will be closed starting at the junction with Gristlehurst Lane and extending 95 metres southward. Due to the nature of the closure, there will be no alternative route for vehicles.

Motorists are advised to plan their journeys accordingly, as the closure may impact traffic flow during the specified hours.

For further details, residents can view a map of roadworks across Greater Manchester on the Rochdale Borough Council website.

articles.title: Hopwood Triangle Traffic Trial to Continue Pending Township Vote
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council has confirmed that the Hopwood Triangle traffic calming trial will remain in place until a formal township vote is conducted to decide its future.
articles.content_html:
A traffic calming trial at the Hopwood Triangle in Heywood will continue pending a formal vote by the township, Rochdale Council has announced. The trial has faced criticism from motorists and residents and introduced several changes to the roads, including the closure of Middleton Road at its junction with Manchester Road near St John's Church.

Councillor Bev Place, representing North Heywood, expressed disappointment that the trial would not end as soon as she had hoped. She stated that highways officers informed her that a township meeting is required to formally vote on the trial's termination. Councillor Place is working to arrange an extraordinary meeting, as the next scheduled meeting is not until 22nd September.

The trial has implemented measures such as making Magdala Street one-way towards Manchester Road, introducing new HGV parking restrictions, and establishing a 20mph speed limit on surrounding residential roads. Councillor Place noted that while some residents want the trial to continue for a full period, heavy congestion around Magdala Street influenced her call for its removal, citing concerns for the safety of pupils at Hopwood Primary School.

A spokesperson for Rochdale Council stated that there is no set date for the removal of the restrictions and that they are in discussions with contractors regarding the situation. The council also mentioned that traffic modelling is not typically conducted for residential side street schemes, and a live trial is deemed the most effective way to evaluate the impact on traffic and road safety.
